description.value: A perfusion fMRI study of cigarette cue-induced craving in smokers, comparing cerebral blood flow during smoking versus nonsmoking cues and examining correlations with craving.

spans.text: We utilized ASL perfusion fMRI to characterize regional brain activation during cigarette CIC, independent of interference from pharmacological withdrawal.

value: We expected to see greater neural activity to smoking cues in the areas of the pedunculopontine nucleus, ventral tegmental area, and ventral striatum
we hypothesized greater perfusion in the ventral striatum and the interconnected amygdala, anterior and posterior cingulate, select prefrontal regions, hippocampus, and thalamus

We hypothesized that increases in perfusion in ventral medial prefrontal and deep limbic structures (amygdala, insula, and ventral striatum), regions important in mediating responses to drug cues, would correlate with subjective craving scores.
